title: NASA: LOST MISSIONS
subtitle: The first car on another world

story_arc.opening: Apollo 15 was designed for longer lunar stays, longer drives and more science than earlier Apollo missions.
story_arc.turn: The Lunar Roving Vehicle carried astronauts across Hadley-Apennine, helping them reach rocks and terrain far beyond the landing site.
story_arc.ending: The crew returned to lunar orbit, but the rover and the surface experiments stayed behind as a working record of exploration.
story_arc.emotional_line: The rover did not come home. Its tracks and instruments became part of the Moon's permanent human-made landscape.

hardware.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV)
hardware.what_it_was: A lightweight electric vehicle designed for the Moon's low gravity and airless surface.
hardware.why_sent: To extend the astronauts' range and let them investigate more of the Hadley-Apennine region.
hardware.instrument: Navigation system, communications equipment and a television camera used during the traverses.
hardware.discovery: The rover helped the crew reach and document Hadley Rille, the Apennine mountain front and many sample stations.
hardware.why_left: The crew needed to leave the lunar surface in the Lunar Module; the rover was not designed to return to Earth.
hardware.what_remains: Apollo 15's LRV remains parked near the Falcon lunar module landing site on the Moon.

current_status.location: Hadley-Apennine, Moon (near the Falcon landing site)
current_status.status: Inactive and inert; left behind by design
current_status.last_event: Used during Apollo 15 surface traverses in July–August 1971; not powered after the crew departed.

hardware.name: Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
hardware.what_it_was: A group of experiments deployed on the lunar surface after landing.
hardware.why_sent: To keep collecting scientific measurements after the astronauts left the Moon.
hardware.instrument: Seismic, heat-flow, magnetic-field and other lunar-environment experiments.
hardware.discovery: ALSEP data helped scientists study the Moon's interior, surface environment and response to impacts.
hardware.why_left: It was built to operate on the Moon after the crew's short surface visit.
hardware.what_remains: The Apollo 15 experiment package remains at its deployment site near Hadley-Apennine.

current_status.last_event: The Apollo 15 ALSEP was shut down along with the other ALSEP stations on September 30, 1977.

hardware.name: Laser Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR)
hardware.what_it_was: A corner-reflector array deployed as part of Apollo 15's surface experiments.
hardware.why_sent: To reflect laser beams from Earth for precise measurements of Earth–Moon distance and lunar motion.
hardware.instrument: 300 fused-silica corner reflectors in a passive array.
hardware.discovery: Lunar laser ranging with Apollo retroreflectors has supported long-term measurements of the Moon's orbit and related geophysical studies.
hardware.why_left: It is a passive instrument designed to remain on the Moon with no power or crew support.
hardware.what_remains: The retroreflector array remains at the Apollo 15 site on the Moon.

current_status.status: Passive instrument on the lunar surface
current_status.last_event: Deployed during Apollo 15; no powered operations to end. Used in ongoing laser-ranging observations from Earth.

ending.title: You found what Apollo 15 left behind.
ending.tagline: The journey ended. The evidence stayed.
ending.codex_text: Apollo 15 left the first Lunar Roving Vehicle and a surface experiment package at Hadley-Apennine. Together they expanded how far humans could explore and how long science could continue after departure.
